verdict.rationale: TypeSafe publishes its own model-jaggedness page for jev-1.13, which says "Jev isn't perfect" and lists nine failure modes. These include literal reading, math and counting, date-time comparison, indirection, large irrelevant state, adversarial content, contradictory instructions, structural invariants and generation, each with a "Do this instead" mitigation and a last-reviewed date. That directly delivers vendor-authored documentation of what the model is bad at. Missing for 10: no independent or hands-on corroboration that the page is accurate or complete. Community testing reports a choice-reordering probability sensitivity that the listed failure modes do not cover.

support.subject: As a developer, the vendor documents the model's failure modes and jagged edges — what it is bad at, in its own docs, not just what it aces

citations.quote: Jev isn't perfect. Here are some jagged edges we are aware of with jev-1.13

nine documented failure modes (literal reading, math and numbers/counting, date-time comparison, indirection, large state full of irrelevant detail, adversarial content, contradictory instructions, structural invariants, generation), each with a "Do this instead" mitigation
